questions.q: What are the three main parties in an OAuth 2.0 flow?
o: Client, Proxy, Resource Owner
Resource Owner, Client Application, Authorization Server (plus Resource Server)
User, Attacker, Server
Browser, API, Database
questions.x: The Resource Owner is the user. The Client Application is the app requesting access (e.g., a blog). The Authorization Server authenticates the user and issues tokens. The Resource Server holds the protected data.
questions.h: Think about who wants access (the app), who grants it (the user), and who decides if it is allowed (the auth service).

questions.q: What is the authorization code flow?
o: The user's password is hashed and sent to the authorization server directly
The user approves access on the authorization server, which sends a short-lived code to the client, the client then exchanges the code for an access token via a back-channel request
The access token is embedded in the redirect URL after login
The client generates the token locally after verifying the user's credentials
questions.x: The code flow separates user-facing redirects from server-to-server token exchange. The code travels through the browser (visible) but the final access token is obtained back-channel (not visible in the URL), making it harder to intercept.
questions.h: The flow has two steps: a redirect with a code, then a server-side exchange. Why split it into two steps instead of sending the token directly in the redirect?

questions.q: What is the purpose of the state parameter in an OAuth authorization request?
o: It encodes the user's preferred language for the consent screen
It is a random value the client includes to prevent CSRF attacks, it is returned in the redirect and the client verifies it matches
It tells the authorization server how long to keep the session
It contains the list of scopes the client is requesting
questions.x: The state parameter is a CSRF token for the OAuth flow. The client generates a random value, sends it in the authorization request, and when the code comes back in the redirect, the client checks that the state matches what it sent.
